title: Lessons with Professor David Jones
summary: He studied with Professor David Jones, who retaught everything from method books at 50 cents a lesson twice a week.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Did you take any lessons or did you just learn at home? Well, I started playing from around with some of the upper grade musicians. Then I went to Professor David Jones, but they don't accept what somebody else teach you. But then he took me back over everything that they had learnt me to review it. But then I went so fast with it, well he couldn't…you know, he had to accept it.
Can you tell us anything about him? I missed him in California. He's still out there, I guess, still living in California.
Well, David Jones is still out there in California. He's still out there.
What method did he use? Remember books or anything? How he taught?

Well, now, I got some old books, but maybe the back is off them. But you had to go in the method and you had to start out the method. It wasn't the same thing he wanted you to play a song or nothing like that. He wanted you to keep writing in the method.
But you still got those method books?
I got…yeah, I got the…well, the back is off. I still got it back there now.

Yeah, okay, well I'll let you see it in this minute. Yeah, I got several of them back there. So, I like that and I got the catechism when I started. Before I started, well, they gave me a catechism. Well, I had to learn catechism. Well, I learned the music before I learned how to pick up an instrument. Then after that, well, I did start on music. Well, I know all the rudiments and know the notes and the scales and so forth. It was hard, right? No trouble. Then I wanted to do it. Something you want to do would come more faster. Then time was kind of rough. Then I didn't want to pay for the second lesson. That would make me study harder. You understand what I mean? Because I didn't want to pay two or three times for the same lesson. That would make me get the lesson because a dollar was a dollar at that time. So, that made me study harder. Did you charge a dollar a lesson then? Well, at that time I was paying 50 cents, but 50 cents was greater than a dollar.
You had more than a dollar now.

Yeah, so 50 cents meant a lot. So, I didn't want to take a lesson three or four times. I began to count upon what I'd be paying. So, that would make me study hard to get my lesson. So, I didn't want to take my lesson over. So, every time I'd go, well, I'd have my lesson. It took about twice a week.
